themes_detail.label: Garbage Collection Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Missed Collection complaints surged to 11 THIS WEEK vs. a 2.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 340% spike (z-score: 4.12)—indicating a sudden sanitation service breakdown affecting Woodhaven/Richmond Hill residents' ability to dispose of waste.
evidence: 11 Missed Collection complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.5 weekly baseline (340% spike)
Z-score of 4.12 indicates statistically significant deviation
Pattern suggests acute service disruption, not chronic underfunding
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY to determine root cause: staffing shortage, equipment failure, route changes, or weather-related delays
Interview residents about garbage pileup on streets and health/pest implications; photograph visual evidence

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Cutting Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal Tree Damage complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 500% spike (z-score: 3.54)—suggesting either organized tree removal or contractor abuse in the district.
evidence: 3 Illegal Tree Damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (500% spike)
Z-score of 3.54 indicates high statistical significance
Concurrent spike in Dead/Dying Tree complaints (4 last week vs. 1.0 avg, +300%) suggests environmental stress or damage
reporting_angles: Request 311 complaint details to identify geographic clusters or specific addresses; cross-reference with DOB permits to catch unpermitted tree work
Interview Parks Department about enforcement; investigate whether contractors or residents are behind illegal removals

themes_detail.label: Hazardous Materials Spike
themes_detail.summary: Hazardous Materials complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 1100% spike (z-score: 6.35)—indicating potential environmental contamination or illegal dumping events in the district.
evidence: 3 Hazardous Materials complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1100% spike)
Z-score of 6.35 indicates very high statistical significance
Spike suggests acute contamination event rather than baseline exposure
reporting_angles: Obtain specific 311 complaint locations and details; determine what materials were reported and whether violations were issued
Contact EPA, NYC Department of Environmental Protection, and FDNY hazmat to cross-reference incident reports and enforcement actions

themes_detail.label: Dangling Street Signs Safety Risk
themes_detail.summary: Street Sign - Dangling complaints spiked to 6 THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 0.8 weekly average—a 700% spike (z-score: 7.94)—creating potential public safety hazards, though recency has declined since initial surge.
evidence: 6 Street Sign - Dangling complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (700% spike)
Z-score of 7.94 indicates extremely high statistical significance
Spike has moderated in past 2 weeks, suggesting either repairs completed or issue resolved
reporting_angles: Determine whether DOT has fixed the reported signs or if backlog persists; assess response time
Photograph any remaining hazards and document potential injury risks to pedestrians/drivers

themes_detail.label: Animal-Related Complaints Rising
themes_detail.summary: Animal-Abuse complaints rose to 7 LAST WEEK vs. 3.9 weekly average (81% spike, z-score: 2.68), while Dead Animal complaints hit 10 THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 3.5 weekly average (186% spike, z-score: 2.77)—suggesting either increased animal distress or improved resident reporting.
evidence: 7 Animal-Abuse complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.9 weekly baseline (81% spike, z-score: 2.68)
10 Dead Animal complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 3.5 weekly baseline (186% spike, z-score: 2.77)
Community Board has recurring request to enhance animal welfare programs, indicating awareness of district-level concern
reporting_angles: Contact ASPCA and NYC Animal Care & Control to determine whether complaints reflect increased abuse, neglect, or disease
Interview residents about patterns: are animals being abandoned, starved, or dying from environmental conditions (e.g., heat, contamination)?
